categories.name: Control Environment
categories.summary: Tone at the top: ethics, board oversight, structure, competence, accountability.

categories.name: Communication and Information
categories.summary: Getting the right information to the right people, inside and outside the company.

categories.name: Risk Assessment
categories.summary: Identifying what could go wrong — including fraud — and analyzing it.

categories.name: Monitoring Activities
categories.summary: Checking that controls are actually working, and reporting when they are not.

categories.name: Control Activities
categories.summary: Selecting and deploying the controls, including technology controls and policies.

categories.name: Logical and Physical Access
categories.summary: Who can get to what: provisioning, least privilege, encryption, physical access.

categories.name: System Operations
categories.summary: Running the system: vulnerability management, monitoring, incident response.

categories.name: Change Management
categories.summary: Authorizing, testing, and approving changes before they reach production.

categories.name: Risk Mitigation
categories.summary: Staying resilient to business disruptions and vendor failures.

categories.name: Processing Integrity
categories.summary: Processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized.

categories.name: Confidentiality
categories.summary: Confidential information is protected in life and destroyed at end of retention.

outOfScopeCategories.name: Availability
outOfScopeCategories.summary: Capacity, backup, and recovery against uptime commitments.

outOfScopeCategories.name: Privacy
outOfScopeCategories.summary: Notice, choice, collection, retention, disclosure, and quality of personal information.

criteria.intent: The company demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.
The board exercises independent oversight of the system of internal control.
Management establishes reporting lines, structures, and authority to pursue objectives.
The company attracts, develops, and retains competent people.
The company holds individuals accountable for their control responsibilities.
Relevant, quality information is obtained and used to support internal control.
Internal control information, including responsibilities, is communicated internally.
Relevant information is communicated to external parties such as customers.
Objectives are specified clearly enough to identify and assess related risks.
Risks to objectives are identified and analyzed as a basis for managing them.
The potential for fraud is considered when assessing risk.
Changes that could significantly affect internal control are identified and assessed.
Ongoing and separate evaluations confirm whether controls are present and working.
Control deficiencies are evaluated and communicated to those responsible for corrective action.
Control activities are selected and developed to mitigate risks to acceptable levels.
Control activities over technology are selected and developed to support objectives.
Control activities are deployed through policies and the procedures that put them into action.
Logical access security protects information assets from unauthorized use.
Access is registered, authorized, and removed when no longer appropriate.
Access to data and functions is managed based on roles and least privilege.
Physical access to facilities and protected assets is restricted.
Data and software are removed from assets before disposal or reuse.
The system is protected against threats originating outside its boundaries.
Information is protected in transmission, movement, and removal.
Unauthorized or malicious software is prevented from being introduced.
Configuration standards are used to detect vulnerabilities and unauthorized change.
The system is monitored to detect anomalies that indicate a security event.
Security events are evaluated to determine whether they are incidents.
Identified incidents are contained, remediated, and communicated.
The company recovers from identified incidents and applies what it learns.
Changes to infrastructure, data, software, and procedures are authorized, tested, and approved.
The company identifies and mitigates risks from business disruptions.
Risks arising from vendors and business partners are assessed and managed.
Information about processing objectives and data quality is available to users.
Inputs are complete, accurate, and authorized before processing.
Processing itself is complete, accurate, timely, and properly authorized.
Outputs are complete, accurate, and delivered only to the people entitled to them.
Stored information supporting processing is complete, accurate, and timely.
Information designated confidential is identified and protected through its lifecycle.
Confidential information is disposed of when retention requirements end.
